IDN.name: Indonesia
IDN.framework: Indonesia's Ministry of Health regulates medical devices, with distribution overseen by BPOM. Since July 2024, all distributors must obtain Good Distribution Practices (CDAKB) certification. Device classification follows four risk classes. CE marking and FDA clearances facilitate registration. A local authorized distributor is required. Indonesia is an IMDRF Affiliate Member through its Ministry of Health.

MYS.name: Malaysia
MYS.framework: Malaysia's Medical Device Authority (MDA) regulates medical devices under the Medical Device Act 2012. Devices are classified into four risk classes (A-D). As of 2024, only recognised QMS standards are accepted for registration. CE marking and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence. Malaysia is piloting an accelerated registration program with Singapore HSA for 2025-2026.

CHL.name: Chile
CHL.framework: Chile's ISP regulates medical devices. Registration requires conformity assessment and device classification aligned with international standards. CE and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence for registration.

BOL.name: Bolivia
BOL.framework: AGEMED issues Sanitary Registrations. Requires apostilled documents like CFS and CE/FDA.

PER.agencyFullName: General Directorate of Medicines, Supplies and Drugs
PER.framework: Registration heavily facilitated by providing FSCs from high surveillance countries like USA or EU members.
PER.name: Peru

ARG.agencyFullName: National Administration of Drugs, Foods and Medical Devices
ARG.framework: MDSAP affiliate. Generally relies on approvals from highly regulated countries (US, EU, Japan, etc).
ARG.name: Argentina

CYP.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
CYP.name: Cyprus
CYP.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

IND.framework: Transitioning to comprehensive medical device rules. CDSCO accepts CE/FDA as strong supporting documentation.
IND.name: India

CHN.framework: NMPA strictly regulates all classes. Requires localized clinical data and testing heavily.
CHN.name: China

ISR.name: Israel
ISR.agencyFullName: Medical Technology, Health Information, Innovation and Research Directorate (AMAR), Ministry of Health
ISR.framework: Israel's AMAR (Ministry of Health) regulates medical devices through three registration routes: Declaration (Class I), Fast-Track (Class II), and Normal (Class III+). The framework leverages approvals from recognised reference countries including the US (FDA), EU (CE marking), UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. A local Israeli Registration Holder (IRH) with ISO 9001 certification is required. Fast-Track registrations take 45-60 business days; Normal route takes approximately 120 days.

PSE.name: Palestine
PSE.framework: Regulated by the General Administration of Pharmacy. Registration requires local representation and heavily relies on stringent regulatory authority approvals like CE marking or FDA clearance along with a Certificate of Free Sale.

LBN.name: Lebanon
LBN.framework: Implantable devices require full registration, while non-implantable devices need shipment import permits. The MoPH relies on international standards (CE, FDA) and requires an Authorized Representative.

ETH.name: Ethiopia
ETH.framework: The EFDA regulates medical devices in Ethiopia. Controls include product registration, facility licensing, and import permits. Ethiopia has one of the more developed regulatory frameworks in East Africa and participates in WHO capacity-building programs.

SSD.name: South Sudan
SSD.framework: DFCA regulates medical products and devices in South Sudan.

SOM.name: Somalia
SOM.framework: MOH oversees health product imports and registration in Somalia.

KEN.name: Kenya
KEN.framework: The Pharmacy and Poisons Board (PPB) regulates medical devices in Kenya. Classification follows GHTF/IMDRF guidelines (Class A-D). Registration requires technical dossiers and proof of quality certification (ISO 13485). Kenya is active in EAC harmonization.

MWI.name: Malawi
MWI.framework: PMRA regulates medical devices in Malawi through registration.

TZA.name: Tanzania
TZA.agencyFullName: Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority
TZA.framework: TMDA is one of first agencies in Africa to achieve WHO Maturity Level 3. It regulates medical devices through registration, inspection, and post-market surveillance. Tanzania leads harmonization efforts in the East African Community (EAC).

SYR.name: Syria
SYR.framework: Requires a local authorized representative. Registration involves technical dossiers and a Certificate of Free Sale, and relies on international standards like CE mark and FDA approval.

SUR.name: Suriname
SUR.framework: Requires local distributors to hold permits. Devices must be approved by stringent stringencies (CE/FDA).

GUY.name: Guyana
GUY.framework: Registration primarily relies on reference countries like US FDA, Canada, or CE Europe.

KOR.name: South Korea
KOR.agencyFullName: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
KOR.framework: MFDS regulates medical devices under the Medical Devices Act. Devices are classified into four classes (I-IV). MFDS conducts its own technical review and does not directly accept CE or FDA clearances, though they may support applications. A Korean authorized representative (KAR) is required. South Korea joined the IMDRF Management Committee in December 2017.

PRK.name: North Korea
PRK.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

MAR.name: Morocco
MAR.agencyFullName: Direction du Médicament et de la Pharmacie
MAR.framework: The DMP under the Ministry of Health regulates medical devices in Morocco. Law No. 84-12 governs the registration and control of devices. Registration certificates are valid for 5 years, and foreign manufacturers must appoint a local company for distribution.

ESH.name: Western Sahara
ESH.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

CRI.name: Costa Rica
CRI.framework: Registration via Registrilo requires CFS. High-risk devices heavily rely on FDA, CE, or Health Canada.

NIC.name: Nicaragua
NIC.framework: Registration requires a formalized Certificate of Free Sale. FDA or CE are generally accepted.

COG.name: Congo
COG.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
COG.framework: DPML regulates medical devices through registration and import licensing. A new Conformity Assessment Program (PCEC) was introduced on 1 May 2022, which often uses existing compliance documents like CE marking. FDA clearance (510(k)) is considered high-level documentation that can help speed up the registration process, but it does not bypass the requirement for local registration.

COD.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
COD.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
COD.framework: DPM regulates medical devices in the DRC through product registration.

BTN.name: Bhutan
BTN.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

UKR.name: Ukraine
UKR.agencyFullName: State Service of Ukraine on Medicines and Drugs Control
UKR.framework: Since 2015, Ukraine has operated a conformity assessment system harmonised with EU Directives (MDD 93/42/EEC, AIMD 90/385/EEC, IVDD 98/79/EC). Medical devices require conformity assessment by designated Ukrainian conformity assessment bodies and a national conformity mark. The system mirrors EU risk-based classification (Class I, IIa, IIb, III). Foreign manufacturers must appoint a Ukrainian authorised representative. QMS compliance with ISO 13485 is mandatory for most device classes.

BLR.name: Belarus
BLR.agency: Ministry of Health / Republican Unitary Enterprise
BLR.framework: Belarus is a member of the EAEU and follows the Union technical regulations for medical devices (TR EAEU 017/2013). Devices require mandatory conformity assessment and a Single Registration Certificate valid across all EAEU states. CE and FDA clearances support technical dossiers but do not replace EAEU registration.

NAM.name: Namibia
NAM.framework: NMRC regulates medical devices under the Medicines and Related Substances Control Act. They primarily focus on the registration of high-risk devices and licensing of distributors in the SADC region.

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.agencyFullName: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority
ZAF.framework: SAHPRA regulates medical devices transitioning to full registration. Entities that manufacture, distribute, or wholesale medical devices must obtain a Medical Device Establishment License (MDEL) via SAHPRA, requiring an Authorised Representative and QMS (ISO 13485).

MAF.name: Saint Martin
MAF.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

SXM.name: Sint Maarten
SXM.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

OMN.name: Oman
OMN.agencyFullName: Ministry of Health, Drug Safety Center
OMN.framework: Oman's Ministry of Health Drug Safety Center regulates medical devices. The country follows GCC harmonization standards. CE and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence. Oman is an IMDRF Affiliate Member through its participation in the Medical Device Control Department.

UZB.name: Uzbekistan
UZB.framework: Medical devices require mandatory registration via Uzfarmagentstvo. CE/FDA strongly preferred.

KAZ.name: Kazakhstan
KAZ.framework: Mandatory registration according to EAEU standards. CE and FDA clearances strongly support technical dossiers.

TJK.name: Tajikistan
TJK.framework: Requires import licensing. Reference clearances like CE and FDA significantly streamline the state registration process.

LTU.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
LTU.name: Lithuania
LTU.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

BRA.framework: ANVISA oversees registration. MDSAP audits strongly substitute for ANVISA specific inspections. Under IN 290/2024, FDA clearances or premarket approvals (PMA) for high-risk devices can be leveraged. Under recent regulations (RDC 751/2022), ANVISA allows for simplified, faster review for devices with approval from recognized foreign regulatory authorities, including CE marking
BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.mra: None currently operational for Medical Devices

URY.name: Uruguay
URY.framework: Importation requires registration. Relies significantly on FDA, CE mark, or MERCOSUR approvals.

MNG.name: Mongolia
MNG.framework: Medical devices are regulated by the Ministry of Health and MASM. Registration requires a local authorized representative and technical dossier. Clearance from stringent regulatory authorities such as CE/FDA is heavily referenced to expedite registration.

RUS.agencyFullName: Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare
RUS.framework: Mandatory national registration or harmonized EAEU registration. High barriers regardless of foreign approvals.
RUS.name: Russia

CZE.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
CZE.name: Czechia
CZE.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

DEU.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
DEU.name: Germany
DEU.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

EST.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
EST.name: Estonia
EST.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

LVA.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
LVA.name: Latvia
LVA.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

SWE.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
SWE.name: Sweden
SWE.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

FIN.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
FIN.name: Finland
FIN.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

VNM.name: Vietnam
VNM.agencyFullName: Ministry of Health, Department of Medical Equipment and Health Works
VNM.framework: Vietnam's Ministry of Health regulates medical devices under Decree 98/2021/ND-CP. Devices are classified into four classes (A-D) aligned with ASEAN harmonization. CE marking and FDA clearances facilitate the registration process. A local authorized representative is required.

KHM.name: Cambodia
KHM.framework: Cambodia's DDF regulates medical devices based on the ASEAN Medical Device Directive (AMDD). Registration via Prakas No. 1258 involves a risk-based classification (A-D). A local registered company must act as the applicant for registration and importation.

LUX.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
LUX.name: Luxembourg
LUX.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

ARE.name: United Arab Emirates
ARE.framework: MOHAP regulates medical devices through its Drug Control Department. Devices are classified per GHTF standards (Class I-IV). A UAE-based Authorized Representative is required for foreign manufacturers. Site registration with MOHAP is mandatory before device registration. CE marking and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence. Registration validity is 5 years. Review takes 4-6 weeks for Class I/II and 8-10 weeks for Class III/IV devices.

BEL.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
BEL.name: Belgium
BEL.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

GEO.name: Georgia
GEO.agency: National Agency for Pharmacy and Quality Control (NAPQC)
GEO.framework: NAPQC regulates medical devices under the Law on Medicines and Pharmaceutical Activities. The framework recognizes stringent foreign approvals as a basis for simplified registration. CE marking and FDA clearances actively facilitate local market authorization.

MKD.name: North Macedonia
MKD.framework: Regulated by MALMED. Deeply aligned with EU MDR. CE mark is strictly accepted and predominantly required.

ALB.name: Albania
ALB.framework: As an EU candidate, Albania harmonizes closely with EU MDR/IVDR. CE mark is universally accepted.

AZE.name: Azerbaijan
AZE.framework: The Analytical Expertise Center under the Ministry of Health regulates the import and registration of medical devices in Azerbaijan. Registration involves a review of technical files and quality certificates (ISO 13485). CE marking is highly recognized during the evaluation process.

TUR.name: Turkey
TUR.agencyFullName: Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency
TUR.framework: Turkey's medical device regulations are fully harmonised with the EU MDR (2017/745) and IVDR (2017/746) under the EU-Turkey Customs Union Agreement. CE marking is mandatory for market access, and certificates issued by EU Notified Bodies are accepted. All devices must also be registered in the Ürün Takip Sistemi (ÜTS), Turkey's national product tracking system. Turkish-language Instructions for Use are required. EU manufacturers may place CE-marked devices on the Turkish market under the Customs Union without a separate Turkish authorised representative.

ESP.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
ESP.name: Spain
ESP.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

LAO.name: Laos
LAO.framework: The FDD under the Ministry of Health regulates medical devices in Laos, aligning with the ASEAN Medical Device Directive (AMDD). New regulations effective January 2024 mandate registration for Class B, C, and D devices and notification for Class A devices.

KGZ.name: Kyrgyzstan
KGZ.framework: Relies heavily on EAEU regulations and EAC mark. Accepts CE and FDA.

ARM.name: Armenia
ARM.agencyFullName: Scientific Centre of Drug and Medical Technology
ARM.framework: Armenia regulates medical devices through the SCDM. As a member of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), Armenia is transitioning to the unified EAEU regulatory framework for medical devices, which includes standardized classification and registration procedures across member states.

DNK.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
DNK.name: Denmark
DNK.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

LBY.name: Libya
LBY.framework: The Ministry of Health oversees the import and use of medical devices. Due to historical transitions, regulatory oversight is primarily focused on centralized procurement and essential product supply chains.

TUN.name: Tunisia
TUN.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
TUN.framework: DPM in Tunisia regulates medical devices through technical evaluation and registration. Devices must comply with safety standards, and CE marking is a standard requirement for imported products.

ROU.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
ROU.name: Romania
ROU.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

HUN.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
HUN.name: Hungary
HUN.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

SVK.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
SVK.name: Slovakia
SVK.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

POL.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
POL.name: Poland
POL.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

IRL.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
IRL.name: Ireland
IRL.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

GBR.agencyFullName: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
GBR.framework: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) regulates medical devices in Great Britain under the UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (as amended). Post-Brexit, the UKCA mark is the domestic conformity route, though CE marking remains accepted under transitional provisions extended to 30 June 2030. The MHRA is developing an international reliance framework that may recognise FDA and other international approvals from 2027, but this is not yet in force. MHRA registration and a UK-based Responsible Person are required for all devices.
GBR.name: Great Britain

GRC.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
GRC.name: Greece
GRC.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

ZMB.name: Zambia
ZMB.framework: ZAMRA regulates medical devices under the Medicines and Allied Substances Act. The agency focuses on registration and licensing to ensure quality and safety. Zambia participates in the SADC ZaZiBoNa collaborative procedure.

SLE.name: Sierra Leone
SLE.framework: PMB regulates medical devices through registration and inspection.

GIN.name: Guinea
GIN.agencyFullName: Direction Nationale de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
GIN.framework: DNPM regulates pharmaceutical and medical device sectors in Guinea.

LBR.name: Liberia
LBR.agencyFullName: Liberia Medicines and Health Products Regulatory Authority
LBR.framework: LMHRA regulates medical devices through registration and quality control.

CAF.name: Central African Republic
CAF.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
CAF.framework: DPM oversees the import and distribution of medical devices.

SDN.name: Sudan
SDN.framework: The NMPB in Sudan regulates medical devices through product registration and establishment licensing. Classification is risk-based, often referencing GHTF standards. Registration involves a review of quality certifications and technical documentation.

DJI.name: Djibouti
DJI.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
DJI.framework: DPM oversees the quality and registration of medical devices.

ERI.name: Eritrea
ERI.framework: DCA regulates medical devices through import controls and registration.

AUT.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
AUT.name: Austria
AUT.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

IRQ.name: Iraq
IRQ.framework: The Ministry of Health (MOH) and KIMADIA regulate medical devices in Iraq. Devices are classified into four risk classes (A-D). Registration requires a local agent and documentation in Arabic. The process often involves technical reviews of safety and performance data.

ITA.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes. The EU is a founding member of the IMDRF.
ITA.name: Italy
ITA.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

CHE.framework: Previously harmonized with EU, now requires a Swiss Rep. Legislated to allow FDA clearance reliance.
CHE.name: Switzerland

IRN.name: Iran
IRN.agencyFullName: Iranian Medical Device Administration / Iran Food and Drug Administration
IRN.framework: The National Medical Device Directorate (NMDD) under the IFDA regulates the market in Iran. Devices are classified into four risk classes (A-D) following GHTF principles. Registration requires a local authorized representative and adherence to quality systems like ISO 13485.

NLD.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
NLD.name: Netherlands
NLD.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

LIE.name: Liechtenstein
LIE.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).
LIE.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices, via EEA); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices, via EEA); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, via EEA)

CIV.name: Côte d'Ivoire
CIV.framework: The AIRP regulates medical devices in Côte d'Ivoire. It enforces product registration and licensing of health product distributors, contributing to UEMOA regional harmonization guidelines.

SRB.name: Serbia
SRB.framework: Medical devices regulated through ALIMS. Fully recognizes CE marking to facilitate localized registration.

MLI.name: Mali
MLI.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
MLI.framework: DPM regulates medical devices through registration and import monitoring.

SEN.name: Senegal
SEN.framework: Senegal's ARP has achieved WHO Maturity Level 3. It regulates medical devices through registration and rigorous post-market surveillance. Senegal is a key player in West African pharmaceutical harmonization.

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.agencyFullName: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
NGA.framework: NAFDAC regulates medical devices in Nigeria using a risk-based classification system. Nigeria has achieved WHO Maturity Level 3 for medicines and is a leader in regional harmonization via the ECOWAS JAP. Foreign manufacturers must appoint a local authorized representative.

BEN.name: Benin
BEN.framework: ABRP regulates medical devices through registration and inspection.

AGO.name: Angola
AGO.agencyFullName: Agência Reguladora de Medicamentos e Tecnologias de Saúde
AGO.framework: Angola's ARME oversees the regulation of health products. While pharmaceutical regulation is established, medical device specific frameworks are currently being strengthened to improve quality oversight and import controls.

HRV.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
HRV.name: Croatia
HRV.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

SVN.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
SVN.name: Slovenia
SVN.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

QAT.name: Qatar
QAT.framework: Qatar's Ministry of Public Health regulates medical devices. The country follows GCC harmonization standards for device classification and registration. A local authorized representative is required. CE marking and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence for registration. Qatar is working towards implementing the GCC Medical Device Passport for harmonized regional approvals.

SAU.name: Saudi Arabia
SAU.framework: The SFDA regulates medical devices under the Medical Devices and Supplies Regulation. All devices require a Medical Device Marketing Authorization (MDMA). Devices are classified into four risk-based classes (A-D), aligned with GHTF/IMDRF standards. A Saudi Authorized Representative is required. ISO 13485 QMS certification is mandatory. The SFDA accepts CE marking and FDA clearances as supporting evidence but conducts its own technical review. Registration typically takes 3-6 months.

BWA.name: Botswana
BWA.framework: BoMRA regulates medical devices through registration and listing procedures. Botswana is an active member of the SADC ZaZiBoNa harmonization initiative and was one of the first IMDRF Affiliate Members in Africa.

ZWE.name: Zimbabwe
ZWE.framework: MCAZ regulates medical devices through registration and monitoring.

PAK.name: Pakistan
PAK.framework: Medical devices in Pakistan are regulated by DRAP under the Medical Device Rules 2017. Devices are classified into Class A, B, C, and D based on risk. Registration is mandatory, and foreign manufacturers must appoint a local authorized representative (LAR). Establishments must also hold a valid license to import.

BGR.framework: Regulated under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) and IVDR. Requires CE marking via Notified Bodies for most classes.
BGR.name: Bulgaria
BGR.mra: EU-Australia MRA (Medical Devices); EU-New Zealand MRA (Medical Devices); EU-Switzerland MRA (Medical Devices, Chapter 4)

THA.name: Thailand
THA.agencyFullName: Food and Drug Administration, Ministry of Public Health
THA.framework: Thailand's FDA regulates medical devices under the Medical Device Act B.E. 2551 (2008). Devices are classified into four risk classes. Since 2024, an Abridged Pathway offers expedited registration for devices already approved by recognised reference agencies (TGA, US FDA, EU Notified Bodies, MHLW, Health Canada, WHO PQ IVD). GMP compliance is mandatory for moderate-to-high-risk device manufacturers. ISO 13485 certification is accepted.

SMR.name: San Marino
SMR.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

HTI.name: Haiti
HTI.framework: Regulatory mechanisms are minimal; relies overwhelmingly on foreign source clearances like FDA and CE.

DOM.name: Dominican Republic
DOM.framework: Requires Sanitary Registration. Accepts FDA 510k and CE Marks as substantial equivalent benchmarks.

TCD.name: Chad
TCD.agencyFullName: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament
TCD.framework: DPML regulates health product imports and registration in Chad.

KWT.name: Kuwait
KWT.framework: Kuwait's Food and Drug Authority regulates medical devices following GCC harmonization guidelines. Devices must be registered before market placement. CE marking and FDA clearances are accepted as supporting evidence. A local authorized representative is required.

SLV.name: El Salvador
SLV.framework: DNM oversees imports. Foreign manufacturers must appoint a local legal rep. CFS or FDA/CE is required.

GTM.name: Guatemala
GTM.framework: Medical devices must be registered with the Department of Registration. CFS is mandatory. CE mark or FDA clearances help.

TLS.name: East Timor
TLS.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

BRN.name: Brunei
BRN.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

MCO.name: Monaco
MCO.framework: Specific regulatory framework data is unavailable, decentralized, or heavily relies on importing from recognized reference nations (e.g., EU, USA).

DZA.name: Algeria
DZA.framework: Algeria's ANPP regulates the registration and commercialization of medical devices. Recent reforms have strengthened the technical evaluation process. Conformity certificates or CE marks are generally required for registration of imported devices.

MOZ.name: Mozambique
MOZ.framework: ANARME regulates medical devices through registration and licensing. Mozambique participates in regional SADC joint assessment programs to improve regulatory efficiency and product access.

SWZ.name: Eswatini
SWZ.framework: The Ministry of Health oversees health product regulation in Eswatini.

BDI.name: Burundi
BDI.agencyFullName: Autorité Burundaise de Régulation des Médicaments
BDI.framework: ABREMA regulates the pharmaceutical sector and medical devices in Burundi.

RWA.name: Rwanda
RWA.framework: Rwanda FDA attained WHO Maturity Level 3 in 2024. It regulates medical devices through establishment licensing, product registration, and control of clinical trials. The agency is highly digitalized and efficient.

MMR.name: Myanmar
MMR.framework: Myanmar's FDA regulates medical devices according to the ASEAN Medical Device Directive (AMDD) standards. Devices are classified into four risk categories (A-D). Registration requires a local representative and a Certificate of Registration from the country of origin.
